checklist.notes: The language and task demands in the A1-U01-L02 LESSON are broadly appropriate for its declared CEFR tier.
No material English grammar, lexical, pronunciation-description, or meaning error was found in the reviewed A1-U01-L02 LESSON.
The lesson asks learners to construct and analyze “Did you say leave?” before past simple is introduced, rather than clearly presenting it as an unanalyzed clarification chunk.
The practice directions operationalize a did-question while the declared grammar target is present simple, so the linguistic scope and task protocol do not agree.
The learner-facing English in the A1-U01-L02 LESSON is sufficiently clear and natural for the declared tier.

No suspiciously distinctive copied passage is apparent in the short A1-U01-L02 LESSON, but internal inspection cannot establish originality beyond the retained project evidence and no Internet-wide comparison was performed.

findings.description: The lesson explicitly uses a past-simple auxiliary question before concept_past_simple is introduced in the following lesson.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with an in-scope clarification pattern or explicitly authorize and teach the prerequisite before requiring construction.

limitations: This review covers only the immutable A1-U01-L02 LESSON and its fresh static machine-report context. It does not assess human or release approval, provider authentication, live-provider behavior, learner outcomes, or Internet-wide originality.
